To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we have designed and synthesized new peptide conjugates of lactoterricin analogs and antimicrobals; 2) we found that the conjugates are active against Gram positive bacteria and Candida yeast; 3) we found that conjugates are less cytotoxic than antibiotics used in therapies.
the novel antimicrobial conjugates composed of lactoferrin-derived peptides and fluoroquinolones or azole derivatives were designed and synthesized.

the new peptide conjugates containing modified bovine lacto ferricin analogues (LFcins) and the antimicrobials CIP, LVX and FLC are active against Candida yeast and Gram positive bacteria and exert a low cytotoxic effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of novel peptidic compounds with antimicrobial properties, which are potentially useful for the development of new therapeutic agents.
the design and development of novel antimicrobials based on peptide conjugates.
a new class of antimicrobial agents that are composed of a peptide and an active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) and that are designed to overcome the problem of antibiotic resistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented approach is a promising strategy to design and synthesize novel antimicrobial agents.
the presented conjugates can be considered as potential candidates for further development of new antimicrobial compounds.
the proposed peptide conjugates are potential candidates for the development of new antimicrobial agents with a broad spectrum of action.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed peptide-antimicrobial conjugates can be considered as a novel class of antimicrobials with potential therapeutic use.
the presented conjugates can serve as a promising basis for the development of new antimicrobial agents.
the proposed conjugate compounds are a good alternative to antibiotics, especially for the treatment of Candida yeast infections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to design and synthesize peptidic compounds with antimicrobial properties that can be used as a template for the development of new drugs with reduced toxicity.
it is possible to design novel peptide conjugates with improved antimicrobial activity and reduced toxicity.
the proposed conjugate design can be used for the development of new drugs with improved properties.
